source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    Enter BMC Web UI -> Click tab "Dashboard"
And also enter "Server Health" -> "Sensor Reading"

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.

original_test_intent: Verify the four temperature records represented by `TEMP_GB_PCB1~4`—presumptively PCB temperature zones or probes 1 through 4 on the GPU baseboard—are individually readable in Dashboard and Server Health > Sensor Reading with correct physical-zone identity, value, units, status and supported thresholds for the approved board specification.
original_method: Confirm GB/PCB terminology, resolve four stable BMC records, bind each PCB index to its physical baseboard zone or sensor component using the approved schematic/layout and management path, then compare complete passive raw/UI fields with per-zone limits under recorded system power, GPU/baseboard load and cooling conditions. Preserve logs and airflow/hardware state.
manual_activity: The platform owner confirms GB/PCB semantics, maps PCB1-4 to four physical board zones or probes and their BMC management sources, and supplies per-zone limits. Automation can collect four BMC records and both UI views; a human resolves zone/placement/source ambiguity and owns the verdict. No GPU load, board service, airflow/fan manipulation or threshold stimulus is authorized.
required_inputs: Exact chassis/GPU-baseboard PN and revision, BMC/BIOS build and confirmation of GB/PCB terminology
Per-index PCB1-4 schematic/layout location, named zone or monitored component, sensor part/type and measurement point
BMC management source for each temperature, including controller, bus, mux, device address and exact field
Stable SDR name/number/type/entity/instance and Dashboard/Server Health row for every PCB1-4 sensor
Per-zone units, scaling/rounding, tolerance, threshold capability/values/hysteresis, health and freshness specification
Recorded system power state, GPU/baseboard workload, fan mode/speeds, inlet/ambient and chassis airflow configuration
Any approved non-intrusive reference-temperature location and tolerance, without opening the chassis or disturbing airflow
Validated ipmitool/API/browser versions, protected authentication and pinned reviewed `sensor.git` revision/checksum or manual method
safety_requirements: Do not clear SEL, kernel, GPU or thermal logs; existing events and trends are relevant evidence despite the generic Master precondition.
Do not issue `sensor get 'TEMP_GB_PCB1~4'` unless that exact string is documented as one record. Enumerate and query PCB1 through PCB4 separately and preserve each identity and status.
Do not map PCB index to GPU slot, NVSwitch or OS enumeration without schematic evidence. A PCB-zone thermistor can reflect local board temperature rather than a device die.
Treat I2C/I3C/management access as BMC/platform scope. Require controller/bus/mux/address and exact field; host GPU telemetry alone does not prove the BMC board-zone value.
Do not start GPU workload or thermal stress, open or service the baseboard, place probes without approval, alter airflow/fans/thresholds or flash firmware. Record the current passive condition.

Do not truncate inventory, expose passwords with `-P`, assume cipher 17 or execute the unavailable Script. Stop without automatic retry on missing/duplicate/swapped zones, stale data or raw/UI/spec disagreement.
agent_execution_scope: Validate target, GB/PCB definitions, baseboard schematic/zone/BMC-bus map, client and Script; build a four-zone expectation matrix before collection.
Retrieve PCB1-PCB4 independently with complete SDR identity, value, units, supported thresholds, status and timestamp; capture each unchanged Dashboard and Server Health row.

Correlate each record with a physical board zone or sensor component and the recorded power/load/fan/airflow condition; use an external reference only if its exact location and non-intrusive method are approved.
Preserve raw/redacted evidence and logs; perform no clear, GPU/thermal load, chassis opening, probe placement, airflow/fan/threshold/firmware change, automatic retry or DUT verdict.
engineer_actions: Confirm GB/PCB semantics and approve the four-zone physical, schematic and BMC management-source map.
Provide per-zone thermal limits, tolerance, threshold/status/freshness rules and any approved reference-measurement method; approve the collection tool/Script.
Review PCB1 through PCB4 independently and issue the formal verdict without using GPU die, NVSwitch or aggregate board evidence as a substitute.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Unfit as written because tilde shorthand is not an IPMI wildcard and one response cannot prove four PCB-zone records. It omits schematic zone, sensor-source and UI/spec mapping, truncates fallback data, exposes credentials and assumes cipher support.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Enumerate complete sensors, confirm four baseboard PCB-zone identities and BMC telemetry sources, resolve every vendor-supported record and query it through protected read-only access, then correlate four UI rows with the approved physical-zone matrix.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: TEMP_GB_PCB1~4, Dashboard and Server Health > Sensor Reading, readability/specification Criteria, generic clear text, Script URL, DeepSeek commands and 1/0-minute estimates remain preserved; Review expands the range without editing Master or introducing workload/threshold stimulus.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use a four-row matrix keyed by physical GPU-baseboard PCB zone or probe and stable BMC sensor, documenting schematic location, sensor part/measurement point and management bus/source, then compare complete raw/API and UI fields with per-zone limits under a recorded passive power/load/cooling state.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: The exact GPU-baseboard population/revision and BMC/SDR/WebUI build documented by the Project.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record chassis/GPU-baseboard, BIOS/BMC/SDR/WebUI, GPU driver/firmware if used only for inventory, management client and Script revisions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: GPU-baseboard schematic/layout and PCB-zone index map, sensor-device definition, BMC management-bus/SDR specification, thermal limits, WebUI schema and Project configuration specification.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Resolves a range into four physical PCB-zone-bound records and adds schematic/management-source evidence while preserving passive display coverage.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Static PCB-zone temperatures do not validate GPU or NVSwitch die temperature, workload response, threshold assertion/deassertion, fan-control or shutdown policy; those remain separate coverage.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: GB/PCB zone and BMC-source map, per-zone acceptance, passive-state timing rules, protected tool or reviewed Script and evidence contract.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: PCB numbering can differ between schematic, silkscreen, SDR and UI; sensors may be board-local thermistors with placement-dependent gradients, and UI polling can lag.

project_override_considerations: A Project may use Redfish/OEM board telemetry or an approved calibrated reference as an alternative/corroboration only while preserving the original ipmitool method, recording interface/version/field or probe location and reason, obtaining engineer approval and proving equivalent separate PCB1-4 identity, value, threshold, status and freshness coverage. GPU/NVSwitch die temperature is not automatically equivalent to a PCB-zone sensor.
expected_evidence: Chassis/GPU-baseboard PN/revision, BMC/BIOS, confirmed GB/PCB terminology and four-row schematic location, named zone/sensor-component and measurement-point matrix
BMC controller/bus/mux/address and exact temperature-field source for each PCB1-4 record
Complete separate raw records with stable IDs, values, units, threshold capabilities/values, status and timestamps plus separate redacted Dashboard/Server Health rows

Per-zone Project/vendor specification and recorded system power, GPU/baseboard load, fan speeds, inlet/ambient and airflow state with tolerance/update-lag and any approved non-intrusive reference comparison

Explicit missing/duplicate/swapped/stale/divergent disposition, pinned Script/tool security evidence, no-clear/no-load/no-airflow-change/no-service/no-retry proof, final GPU/baseboard/BMC health and engineer-owned four-zone verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The range is unsuitable as a literal query and GB/PCB zones need Project confirmation, but Items, UI Procedure and Criteria consistently request passive display/specification validation of four temperature records. Exact zone, placement and telemetry-source mapping is a readiness input, not a conflicting purpose.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The four-record passive board-temperature purpose is identifiable and plausibly targets four GPU-baseboard PCB zones or probes. Project SPEC can provide the physical map and acceptance limits, so missing inputs do not make the review permanently BLOCKED.

review_improvement: Prevents a failed range query, GPU die/NVSwitch reading or aggregate board value from being presented as four PCB-zone temperatures, and prevents GPU stress, airflow changes or threshold stimulus from being added to a passive display test.
independent_technical_reasoning: A PCB-labeled temperature commonly comes from a board-local thermistor or monitor channel whose result depends on exact placement and airflow, not necessarily from a GPU or switch die. PCB1-4 therefore need schematic-zone and sensor-source mapping before their values can be compared with limits. Passive UI validation provides no authority for workload, invasive probe placement or alarm stimulus.
